chapter: Tenor players, tours and band boys
title: The Mills Blue Rhythm Band that became Lucky Millinder's
summary: Hinton and Francis discuss Irving Mills's band, which Lucky fronted with Red Allen, Higginbotham and Edgar Hayes.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Uh huh. You know what we didn't mention? The Mills Blue Rhythm Band. Now that band was organized by Irving Mills, who was the song publisher and the manager -- and I heard that that band came about because of the success that Cab Calloway was having, and they wanted to follow it up like a second band, and so they all of them got Lucky Millinder, which was a personality like Cab Calloway, talked him into coming with the Mills Band. Was that so?
That's right. That was the Mills Blue Rhythm. That was Reverend Irving Mills's band. He owned that band.
And then finally after Lucky got so famous, then he just took his own name, Lucky Millinder. But it was originally the Mills Blue Rhythm Band featuring Lucky Millinder.
Yeah, that's when Red Allen was in there.
Red Allen, yeah, and J.C. Higginbotham were always in that band together. Edgar Hayes was in that band, too, the piano player.
That's right, a big piano player then. He was the one who made Stardust, didn't he?
